Ingredients:

2 cups masa harina

1 cup of laticoa (a fruit similar to a mango or an orange)

1 cup of water

1-2 tbsp vanilla extract

1 tbsp molasses

2 tbsp cinnamon

2 tbsp sugar

2 tbsp butter

2-3 cups of powdered milk

2 tbsp water

Toppings:

Cinnamon, sugar, and butter (optional)

A drizzle of water if the dough is too dry

Instructions:

1) Mix masa harina and water.  I usually use cold water but that has an adverse effect on the texture of my final product.  Mix well with a spoon and let it sit until it becomes more elastic.

2) Add in vanilla and molasses.  Mix again and try not to spill any of the liquid on the floor.

3) Cover the dough and set aside in a warm place.  I usually let it sit in the fridge until I get ready to cook it.

4) Preheat the oven to 350.

5) In a large flat pan, melt the butter.  Add in the cinnamon and sugar.  Stir well and set the butter mixture aside.

6) Mix in the powdered milk, water, and vanilla.  Mix well and set aside.

7) Grease a large pot with vegetable oil or cooking spray.

8) Scoop a big spoonful of dough into the pot and form it into something resembling a ball.

9) When it has formed a ball, take your hot butter mixture and dip the dough ball into it, making sure to cover it evenly.  It is important to use hot butter and warm the dough in the butter before adding it, otherwise it will stick.

10) Place the dough ball in the boiling water and simmer for a few minutes until it starts to cook and turn a beautiful golden color.

11) Drain on a serving plate to drain off any remaining water, and sprinkle with cinnamon, sugar and butter, and serve warm.
